f1.quote: Substitution of the empirical Embedded Atom Method (EAM) potential with a Machine Learning Interatomic Potential (MTP) for the liquid phase

f2.quote: replacement of expensive thermodynamic integration (TI) calculations with free energy perturbation (FEP) calculations

f4.quote: Temperature range 2000–2400 K for SRO analysis

f5.quote: Supercell size 12x12x12 (3456 atoms) for MTP training/MD

f6.quote: High-fidelity MTP capable of closely reproducing the ab initio phase-space distribution for multi-component alloys, with training errors < 1 meV/atom.

f7.quote: The FEP method leverages the small variance in energy differences between MTP and DFT to converge free energy rapidly.

f8.quote: The electronic Gibbs energy difference (arising from a DOS gap at the Fermi level) ... act as critical physical contributions shifting the melting temperature.

f9.quote: Solid-state Short-Range Order (SRO) stabilization (~2.4 meV/atom) act as critical physical contributions shifting the melting temperature.

f10.quote: Computational resource savings of 80% (or ~20x speedup) compared to the original TOR-TILD method

f11.quote: free energy differences between the new method and TI < 0.5 meV/atom

f12.quote: melting points shifting by 48–57 K due to electronic excitations
